clue.text: One crew, not a couple

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: not here means the word a is taken away from the crew word

parts.note: a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A tally of sailors: one crew counted, but not a couple of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like part of a count; it is the definition, and 'not a' removes A from TEAM to leave TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a romantic relationship are called an item, so a couple is an item.

clue.text: Darn pants or trousers, say, after skirts in rage

indicators.note: after means the trousers piece comes behind the rage piece
the skirts of a word are its edges, so only the outside letters of rage are used

parts.note: outer letters of rage
pants and trousers are each called a pair, as in a pair of trousers

explanation.surface: Someone angrily mending their trousers, picturing a fit of rage while darning skirts and pants.
explanation.definitionFit: To darn a sock or garment is to mend it, a kind of repair.

clue.text: Fail, as Russian roulette player will wish to do?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to come up with nothing, an idiom for failing

definitions.text: as Russian roulette player will wish to do
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: the player hopes the chamber fired is an empty one, a blank

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for failing to find anything also describes literally getting an empty cartridge in Russian roulette.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a blank is the idiom for getting no result from an attempt, so failing.

clue.text: Fleece pulled up on stormy seas, port found in Ukraine

indicators.note: in a down answer, pulled up means the word is read from the bottom upward, so reversed

parts.note: to fleece someone is to swindle or do them

indicators.note: stormy means the letters of seas are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A fleece hauled aboard on rough seas, at a harbour in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is the major Black Sea port city of southern Ukraine.

clue.text: Instrument lobbed up in wheeze, throwing toys from pram?

indicators.note: in means the reversed instrument goes inside the wheeze word

parts.note: to wheeze is to breathe hard, to pant

indicators.note: in a down answer, lobbed up means the instrument word is sent upward, so reversed

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A tantrum: someone hurling an instrument upward and wheezing like a toddler throwing toys out of the pram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing toys from pram' is a British idiom for a childish tantrum; the question mark marks the definition as a playful example.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing one's toys out of the pram is a sulky childish outburst, the behaviour of someone petulant.

clue.text: See 8
I fail financially to support soldier in legion

indicators.note: in a down answer, the lower piece supports the upper one, so the soldier sits above

parts.note: a soldier is a man in the ranks
a business that fails financially folds

explanation.surface: A soldier in a legion confessing he has gone bust.
explanation.walkthrough: As a definition 'legion' is the adjective meaning very many, as in 'their supporters are legion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are literary adjectives meaning numerous or of many kinds.

clue.text: No chance the Prince of Darkness will slip up then?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for never

definitions.text: the Prince of Darkness will slip up then
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: the Devil would slip on the ice in an underworld turned frozen

explanation.walkthrough: The Prince of Darkness is the Devil; the idiom for 'never' pictures his realm iced over, where he might lose his footing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common idiom for something that will never happen, so no chance.

clue.text: See 28
Online buyer sorry about return of bag

indicators.note: about means the sorry word goes around the other letters

parts.note: 'Sorry?' asking someone to repeat is 'eh?'

indicators.note: return of means the bag word is read backwards

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch

explanation.surface: An online shopper apologises about sending a bag back.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic money is what pays for purchases made on the internet, so it buys things online.

clue.text: Woman shortly, I suspect, delivering the Queen's Speech?

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are rearranged
shortly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the word woman taken as written, then cut

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a woman briefly delivered the monarch's annual address to Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Speech is the British monarch's address opening Parliament, but a queen is also a female cat, whose speech is a mew.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, and the sound a cat makes is its form of speech.

clue.text: Old writer occupying peak in Jerusalem — a mountain!

indicators.note: occupying means the writer sits inside the peak word

parts.note: Sion, or Zion, is the hill in Jerusalem
a quill pen was the old writing instrument

explanation.surface: An ancient author living on Mount Zion in Jerusalem exclaims at the size of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A mountain' is used figuratively, as in 'a mountain of paperwork', meaning a huge number.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge informal number is a vast amount, and a mountain of something means a vast amount.

clue.text: Thinkers arranging beer in line on the counter

indicators.note: in means the rearranged beer goes inside the reversed line
counter suggests counter-direction, so the line word runs backwards

parts.note: an arc is a curved line

indicators.note: arranging means the letters of beer are put in a new order

parts.note: the word beer taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Pub philosophers lining up glasses of beer along the bar counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebra is the plural of cerebrum, the part of the brain that does the thinking.

clue.text: Conservative: I win having lost Conservative city

definitions.note: used attributively, as an adjective: of a city

indicators.note: having lost means the second piece is taken out of the win word

parts.note: a win is a victory
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory boasts of winning, except that the Tory lost the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic means belonging to a town or municipality, the adjective for city matters.

clue.text: Slight lead after a fall, everyone left behind

indicators.note: after means the lead word comes behind the earlier pieces
left behind means those letters are abandoned, removed from the fall word

parts.note: the word fall, which then loses some letters
everyone is all
to be in the lead is to be at the front

explanation.surface: A runner leads after a tumble, leaving the whole field behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' is a noun here, an insult. Removing ALL from FALL leaves F.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub or insult, and an affront is an open insult.

clue.text: Instrument untangling long fur, help Manx

indicators.note: untangling means the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the word help, with its tail cut

explanation.surface: Combing out long fur on a Manx cat, a pet that needs help.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx is a tailless cat breed from the Isle of Man, so the word help loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The flugelhorn is a brass musical instrument similar to a trumpet.

clue.text: Thinner track going uphill, what else can I say?

indicators.note: in a down answer, going uphill means the track word runs bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a rut is a track worn in the ground
PS, the postscript, is what you add when you have more to say

explanation.surface: A slim figure running up a track, lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thinner' looks like a comparative of thin; it is the noun for a paint solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: Turps is the short name for turpentine, a solvent used to thin paint.

clue.text: Painting located in London museum? There you have it!

indicators.note: located in means the painting sits inside the museum letters

parts.note: the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: A lost painting turns up in a London museum, triumphantly announced.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived exclamation announces a reveal, just as 'there you have it' does.

clue.text: Saint terribly worried, terribly worried

indicators.note: terribly means the letters of saint are badly jumbled

parts.note: the word saint taken as written for rearranging
worried as in gnawed: something that worries at you eats at you

explanation.surface: A saint in deep anxiety, the phrase repeated for emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase is read twice: first as an anagram of SAINT plus ATE (worried, as anxiety eats you), then as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a state is an idiom for being very agitated or anxious.

clue.text: Law enforcers satisfied

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ..., London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.walkthrough: The Met is the everyday name for the Metropolitan Police, London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: London's police force is called the Met, and requirements that are satisfied have been fulfilled.

clue.text: Dessert that would come back when booed, did you say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sweet made of baked whipped egg white

definitions.text: that would come back when booed, did you say?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: put boo before the word and it sounds like a curved throwing stick that returns

explanation.walkthrough: Saying 'boo' in front of the dessert's name gives something like 'boomerang', the throwing stick that flies back.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet of whipped egg white and sugar baked crisp is a classic pudding.

clue.text: See 28
Knockout solver?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stunning, excellent thing or person
second meaning: one who cracks a code or puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: A 'cracker' in British slang is something excellent; it is also someone who cracks codes, like this puzzle's solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a stunner, and also a person who breaks codes, just as a solver works out puzzles.

clue.text: See 8
Blood and water etc I had: rinse cut around that

indicators.note: around means the cut rinse word goes around the contraction
cut means the rinse word is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: to rinse out is to flush
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalling washing away blood and water, a grisly cleanup scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood and water are both liquids, things that flow, and examples of the class named.

clue.text: Crystalline mineral unknown, image about right

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

indicators.note: about means the image word goes around right

parts.note: an icon is an image

explanation.surface: An unidentified crystal photographed, with the picture rotated right.
explanation.definitionFit: Zircon is a gem-quality silicate mineral that forms crystals.

clue.text: Capital party for male mogs only, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is said aloud to give the answer's sound

parts.note: a do for cat men: a party is a do, and male mogs are cat men

explanation.surface: An exclusive party where only tomcats are invited.
explanation.walkthrough: A mog, or moggy, is British slang for a cat; 'cat man do' sounds like the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kathmandu is the capital city of Nepal.

clue.text: Fruit that won't take off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the green furry ... fruit
second meaning: the ... bird of New Zealand, which cannot fly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests peeling the fruit's skin; it means flying, which the bird cannot do.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a furry green fruit and to a flightless New Zealand bird.

clue.text: See 26
Musical item with scores reportedly chasing old silent movie star

indicators.note: chasing means the scores piece follows the earlier pieces

parts.note: a harp is a musical instrument

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for scores is said aloud

parts.note: scores are marks, as in exam results

explanation.surface: A musical instrument with its scores pursuing an aged star of silent cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpo was the Marx Brother who never spoke on screen, honking a horn instead.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Marx Brothers comedian whose character never spoke, a mime in sound films.

clue.text: See 8
Forgotten now, carrier of pooh sticks?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for past troubles no longer worth dwelling on
second meaning, read literally: the stream beneath a bridge carries sticks dropped in poohsticks

explanation.walkthrough: Poohsticks, from Winnie-the-Pooh, is a game of dropping sticks off one side of a bridge and seeing whose emerges first downstream.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes past disputes now forgiven, while literally the stream below a bridge carries the sticks.

clue.text: Pink loose robes, crimson when turned round

indicators.note: robes as a verb means clothes, so the loose word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a garment that is loose has been undone

indicators.note: turned round means the crimson word is read backwards

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Pink robes hanging loose, with a crimson one turned inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' looks like a colour beside crimson, but it describes meat cooked lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is pink in the middle has been cooked lightly, not all the way through.
